newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks end off sharply on labor concerns.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks end off sharply on labor concerns.

text.p: Share prices on the Caracas Stock Exchange closed sharply lower across the board in moderate trade Wednesday as investors ran scared of general labor strife and tariff increase delays at national telephone company CANTV, brokers said.
According to preliminary figures from the exchange, the market's 19-share index fell 2.37 percent to 6,061.99 as 29 stocks fell, seven rose and seven closed flat.
"Everybody was selling...There are too many rumors, a climate of instability associated with all the marches and strikes," one broker said.
Thousands of workers and students were due to march against President Rafael Caldera's government in Caracas Wednesday afternoon creating fears of violence.

And CANTV's dispute with the government over a planned second quarter 4.18 percent tariff rise was joined by the announcement Wednesday that the company's unionized employees would go on indefinite strike Thursday over pay.
CANTV closed off 80.00 bolivars at 1,845.00 bolivars.
The composite Merinvest index that includes CANTV fell 2.48 percent to 92.06.
The market's general index is now off 7.5 percent in real terms since the start of the year, compared to rises averaging more than 10 percent in the rest of Latin America.
"We started the year expensive and there have been many reasons not to buy," said Alex Dalmady of Invest Analysis.
A total of 2.774 billion bolivars ($5.8 million) changed hands in 758 trades.
Among heavily traded stocks, Electricidad de Caracas fell 9.25 bolivars to 484.75 bolivars, and steel company Sivensa slipped 1.00 bolivar to 144.00 bolivars.
